# Instant Win Game Card Design and Validation Systems

## Multi-Ticket Sheet Configuration

A printed game card, sheet, or ticket set can be designed to contain multiple individual tickets within a single physical unit. These individual tickets are separated from one another through various methods, including perforation, scoring, or folding techniques. This configuration allows manufacturers and distributors to produce and manage tickets efficiently in bulk while still maintaining the ability to separate them into individual, usable units when needed.

## Individual Ticket Features

Each ticket contained within the larger sheet or card can feature at least one playable instant win game. These games are structured with game indicia—the symbols, numbers, or images that determine winning or losing outcomes—that are concealed beneath a removable layer of material. This covering is typically composed of varnish or a rubber-based substance, which players must scratch off or otherwise remove to reveal the game results. This concealment layer ensures the integrity of the game by preventing premature viewing of outcomes.

## Validation and Activation Indicia

Every individual ticket, regardless of its position within the larger sheet, includes its own unique validation and/or activation indicia. These indicia serve as the mechanism through which a ticket's authenticity and status can be confirmed. Notably, this information can be formatted in multiple ways: it may be designed for human readability, allowing manual verification by staff or automated readability, enabling scanning or electronic processing. In many implementations, tickets are designed with both formats simultaneously, providing flexibility depending on the verification method available at the point of sale or redemption.

## Sheet-Level Activation Option

In addition to individual ticket-level indicia, the overall game card or sheet can incorporate a single, unified activation indicium that applies to the entire sheet. This design enables all individual tickets contained within the sheet to be activated simultaneously at the moment the complete sheet is sold. This approach streamlines the activation process, particularly in scenarios where multiple tickets are sold together as a bundled unit, reducing the need for separate activation steps for each individual ticket.

## Validation Code Processing and Status Determination

When a ticket's validation code is read—whether through manual entry or electronic scanning—the underlying system is capable of performing two critical functions simultaneously. First, it determines whether the ticket is a winning ticket by cross-referencing the validation code against a database of predetermined outcomes. Second, and equally important, the system checks whether the ticket has already been redeemed in a prior transaction. This dual-verification process helps prevent fraud, such as the duplication or reuse of previously validated tickets, while ensuring that legitimate winners receive proper payout confirmation.

# Multi-Ticket Instant Game Card System with Individual Validation and Bulk Activation

## Field of the Invention

This invention relates generally to printed instant-win lottery and promotional game products, and more particularly to a printed game card or sheet configuration comprising multiple perforated tickets, wherein each ticket contains its own instant-win game elements while the entire sheet may be activated as a single unit at the point of sale.

## Background of the Invention

Traditional instant-win game tickets are typically manufactured, distributed, and activated individually. This conventional approach, while straightforward, presents significant inefficiencies for retailers and distributors who must handle, scan, and activate large volumes of individual tickets. Each ticket requires separate handling at the point of sale, creating bottlenecks in high-volume retail environments and increasing the labor and time costs associated with bringing game tickets into active, playable status.

There exists a need in the industry for a system that preserves the integrity and individual identity of each ticket—including its unique winning status, validation history, and redemption record—while streamlining the distribution and activation process to reduce retailer burden and improve operational efficiency.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a printed game card or sheet comprising a plurality of perforated, individually separable tickets, each of which is a complete and independent instant-win game unit. Each individual ticket on the sheet includes:

1. **A concealed game area** protected by a removable covering, such as a scratch-off latex or varnish layer, beneath which is printed the game's outcome (win or lose) and any associated prize information;

2. **A unique validation indicium**, printed in both human-readable form (such as an alphanumeric code) and machine-readable form (such as a barcode, QR code, or similar optical code), which uniquely identifies that specific ticket and allows a central validation system to determine, upon scanning, whether that particular ticket is a winner and whether it has been previously validated or redeemed; and

3. **A unique activation indicium**, similarly rendered in dual human- and machine-readable formats, which is used to bring that specific ticket into an active, playable state within a central gaming or lottery database.

In addition to these individual per-ticket features, the printed sheet itself bears one or more **sheet-wide activation codes**. These sheet-level codes are printed on the sheet in a location distinct from the individual ticket indicia—for example, in a margin, header, or border area of the sheet—and are configured such that a single scan or entry of this code by a retailer's point-of-sale terminal or activation device triggers the simultaneous activation of every individual ticket contained on that sheet. This eliminates the need for a retailer to scan each ticket's individual activation code separately, thereby dramatically reducing the time and effort required to make an entire sheet of tickets available for sale and play.

## Detailed Description

### Sheet and Ticket Construction

The game sheet may be constructed from standard game ticket stock, such as coated paperboard or synthetic paper suitable for the application of scratch-off coatings. The sheet is divided into a plurality of individual ticket sections by perforations, die-cuts, or other separation means, allowing each ticket to be torn away from the sheet and used independently by an end consumer after purchase.

Each individual ticket section, prior to separation, contains all the elements of a complete, self-contained instant-win game, including:

- Game play symbols or numbers concealed beneath a removable covering;
- Prize legend information indicating possible prize amounts or outcomes;
- A unique validation number and corresponding machine-readable code, distinct from that of every other ticket on the sheet and, indeed, distinct from every other ticket ever printed in the game's production run; and
- A unique activation number and corresponding machine-readable code, likewise distinct across the entire ticket population.

### Sheet-Wide Activation Mechanism

The sheet-wide activation code is a separate, distinct code from the individual ticket activation codes. It may be positioned on a header strip, footer strip, or border region of the sheet that remains with the sheet as a whole and is not necessarily separated with individual tickets, or alternatively may be positioned such that it is the last portion of the sheet to be separated from the tickets, ensuring it remains available for scanning during the initial retail transaction.

When a retailer scans this sheet-wide code using a standard point-of-sale terminal connected to a central lottery or gaming server, the central system's database is updated to reflect that every individual ticket associated with that sheet—identified by their unique individual activation codes, which are cross-referenced to the sheet-wide code through a pre-established database association—is now in an "active" and sellable state. This association between the sheet-wide code and the individual ticket codes is established during the printing and data-generation process, prior to distribution of the sheets to retail locations.

### Individual Ticket Validation

Despite the bulk activation of tickets via the sheet-wide code, each individual ticket retains its own unique validation code, which must be independently scanned or entered when a consumer seeks to redeem a potentially winning ticket. Upon receiving a validation request bearing an individual ticket's unique validation code, the central system performs the following determinations:

1. **Winning Status**: The system cross-references the validation code against its database to determine whether the specific ticket is a winning ticket, and if so, the amount or nature of the prize associated with that ticket.

2. **Redemption History**: The system checks whether that specific ticket's validation code has been previously submitted for redemption, thereby preventing duplicate payouts on the same winning ticket—an important fraud-prevention and security feature.

3. **Activation Status**: The system confirms that the ticket, via its association with a sheet-wide activation code, has in fact been properly activated and is therefore eligible for validation and redemption in the first instance.

This dual-layer approach—bulk activation at the sheet level combined with individual validation at the ticket level—allows the benefits of efficient, rapid retail processing to be realized without sacrificing the security, fraud-prevention, and individualized tracking capabilities traditionally associated with single-ticket instant games.

### Advantages of the Invention

This invention offers several notable advantages over prior art systems:

- **Reduced Retail Handling Time**: Retailers can activate an entire sheet of tickets—potentially containing dozens of individual game tickets—with a single scan, rather than scanning each ticket individually.

- **Preserved Security and Integrity**: Despite bulk activation, each ticket maintains its own unique validation and redemption tracking, ensuring that the security protocols essential to lottery and gaming operations remain fully intact.

- **Flexible Distribution**: The sheet format allows for efficient printing, packaging, and distribution of large quantities of tickets as a single physical unit, reducing production and logistics costs.

- **Fraud Prevention**: The individual validation codes, combined with the central database's tracking of redemption history, prevent the same ticket from being redeemed multiple times, even though many tickets were activated together as part of a bulk sheet-activation event.

- **Consumer Experience**: End consumers continue to receive individual, self-contained game tickets that they can separate from the sheet and play independently, preserving the traditional instant-win game experience.

## Conclusion

The described invention represents a significant advancement in the field of instant-win game ticket distribution and activation, striking an effective balance between the operational efficiency demanded by high-volume retail environments and the individualized security and validation integrity required by regulatory and anti-fraud standards in the lottery and gaming industry.

# LOTTERY TICKET SHEET WITH BATCH ACTIVATION AND INDIVIDUAL TICKET VALIDATION

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates generally to instant-win lottery products, and more particularly to a multi-ticket scratch-off sheet construction that permits a plurality of individual lottery tickets to be activated as a single unit at the point of sale while retaining independent, individually verifiable validation data and security features for each constituent ticket.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Conventional instant-win scratch-off lottery tickets are typically manufactured, distributed, and activated on an individual basis. Each ticket carries its own concealed play data beneath a scratch-off layer, and each must be separately scanned or keyed into a point-of-sale ("POS") terminal by a retailer to render it eligible for redemption. While effective for single-ticket transactions, this individualized activation process becomes cumbersome when retailers sell tickets in bulk booklets, strips, or sheets, as is common practice, requiring repeated scanning operations for each ticket prior to sale.

[0003] Existing multi-ticket sheets known in the art generally fall into one of two categories: (a) sheets in which each ticket must be scanned individually for activation, resulting in slow transaction times; or (b) sheets in which a single activation event applies to the entire sheet as an undifferentiated unit, such that individual tickets cannot thereafter be independently tracked, validated, or voided without affecting the remainder of the sheet. The latter approach creates security vulnerabilities, since a lost, stolen, or fraudulently altered ticket cannot be isolated from its siblings for purposes of fraud investigation, partial redemption, or database reconciliation.

[0004] There exists a need for a lottery ticket sheet construction that combines the transactional efficiency of single-scan batch activation with the security and accounting benefits of individualized, independently validated tickets.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0005] The present invention provides a scratch-off lottery ticket sheet comprising a plurality of individual ticket segments joined along frangible (perforated or die-cut) boundaries to a common substrate, together with a dedicated batch-activation zone that is physically and logically distinct from the individual play areas of each ticket.

[0006] Each individual ticket segment includes: (i) a concealed play area printed with unique, pre-randomized prize-determining indicia; (ii) a concealed unique validation code, distinct from that of every other ticket on the sheet and from every other ticket manufactured, printed beneath its own opaque scratch-off coating; and (iii) a visible, pre-printed ticket serial number correlated in a secure remote database to the concealed validation code and to a "batch identifier" shared by all tickets on the sheet.

[0007] The batch-activation zone includes a single concealed batch-activation code, printed beneath a separate opaque scratch-off coating, which, when revealed and transmitted to a central lottery validation system (for example, by retailer scan or key-entry at a POS terminal), causes the system to simultaneously mark as "activated" the database records corresponding to every individual ticket serial number associated with that batch identifier.

[0008] Critically, activation of the batch-activation zone does not reveal, duplicate, or substitute for the individual validation codes of the constituent tickets. Each ticket remains independently interrogable: upon subsequent scratching by a purchaser, the individual validation code is revealed and must be separately submitted to the central system, which will only recognize it as redeemable if (a) the individual ticket's batch identifier corresponds to a batch that has been activated, and (b) the individual ticket's own serial number has not been previously redeemed, voided, or reported. This dual-layer architecture allows an entire sheet to be activated in a single transaction while preserving per-ticket traceability, fraud detection, and independent prize validation.

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0009] **FIG. 1** is a plan view of a multi-ticket lottery sheet according to a preferred embodiment, showing individual ticket segments arranged about a central batch-activation zone.

[0010] **FIG. 2** is a cross-sectional view through an individual ticket segment, illustrating the layered construction including substrate, security layer, printed indicia layer, release coating, and scratch-off latex layer.

[0011] **FIG. 3** is a cross-sectional view through the batch-activation zone, illustrating its analogous but functionally distinct layered construction.

[0012] **FIG. 4** is a schematic block diagram illustrating the data flow between the ticket sheet, a point-of-sale terminal, and a central lottery validation database during batch activation and subsequent individual ticket redemption.

[0013] **FIG. 5** is a flowchart illustrating the method of manufacturing, activating, and validating the ticket sheet.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### A. Physical Construction of the Sheet

[0014] Referring to FIG. 1, a lottery ticket sheet 100 comprises a unitary substrate 102, preferably a paperboard or coated paper stock of basis weight suitable for offset or flexographic printing, upon which are disposed a plurality of individual ticket segments 110a–110n (in the illustrated embodiment, five segments, though the invention is not limited to any particular number) and a single batch-activation zone 120.

[0015] Adjacent ticket segments 110 are separated from one another, and from the batch-activation zone 120, by frangible separation lines 104, which may comprise perforations, micro-perforations, laser-scored lines, or die-cut kiss-cuts of a depth sufficient to permit clean manual or mechanical separation without compromising the structural integrity of the sheet prior to intended separation.

[0016] Each ticket segment 110 comprises, in cross-section as shown in FIG. 2:
- a substrate layer 102;
- an opaque security ink layer 202, optionally incorporating ultraviolet-fluorescent or infrared-readable security taggants, disposed over the substrate;
- a variable-data print layer 204 containing (a) a unique play-data field 206 (prize-determining indicia), (b) a unique individual validation code field 208, printed preferably as an alphanumeric string and a corresponding machine-readable barcode or matrix (QR) code, and (c) a visibly printed, non-concealed ticket serial number 210 and batch identifier 212;
- a release coating layer 206a disposed over the fields to be concealed, to permit clean removal of the overlying layer without damage to the underlying print; and
- an opaque, friable scratch-off layer 208a, typically a latex-based or polymer-based ink formulated to be removable by light abrasion (e.g., with a coin or fingernail) while resisting see-through inspection, light transmission, or solvent/steam disclosure methods.

[0017] The batch-activation zone 120, shown in cross-section in FIG. 3, is constructed analogously, but its concealed print layer 304 contains only a single batch-activation code 306, together with a machine-readable representation thereof (barcode or QR code), and is not associated with any individual prize-determining indicia. The batch-activation zone 120 is preferably positioned at a header or margin region of the sheet 100, distinct from the individual ticket segments, and is dimensioned such that its scratch-off removal by a retailer does not require or induce separation of the individual ticket segments from one another or from the sheet.

### B. Data Architecture

[0018] Referring to FIG. 4, a central lottery validation database 400 maintains, for each manufactured sheet 100, a record associating:
(i) a unique batch identifier 212;
(ii) the corresponding concealed batch-activation code 306, known only to the database and concealed on the physical sheet;
(iii) a list of all individual ticket serial numbers 210 physically printed on ticket segments 110a–110n belonging to that batch;
(iv) for each such serial number, the corresponding concealed individual validation code 208 and associated (also concealed) prize-determining data 206; and
(v) a status flag for the batch (e.g., "manufactured," "distributed," "activated") and an independent status flag for each individual ticket (e.g., "inactive," "eligible," "redeemed," "voided," "flagged-fraud").

[0019] Prior to batch activation, all individual ticket status flags are set to "inactive," rendering them non-redeemable even

# Game Card with Perforated Tickets: Varnish-Covered Indicia and Dual-Code Activation System

**Specification Paragraph:**

The game card comprises a substantially rigid or semi-rigid substrate having a front face and a rear face, said substrate divided by a plurality of perforation lines into a header portion and one or more detachable ticket portions, each detachable ticket portion being separable from the substrate along its respective perforation line without compromising the structural integrity of adjacent ticket portions. Each detachable ticket bears a play area comprising a plurality of latent game indicia—such as symbols, numerals, or alphanumeric characters—printed directly onto the substrate and subsequently obscured by a removable scratch-off varnish layer, said varnish comprising an opaque, friable coating (for example, a crushable latex or polymer-based ink) that may be selectively removed by mechanical abrasion to reveal the underlying indicia without damaging or altering said indicia. In addition to the scratch-off play area, each ticket further comprises a distinct, non-latent activation code and a separately positioned validation code, both printed in plain, non-obscured text or machine-readable format (such as a barcode, QR code, or alphanumeric string), wherein the activation code is unique to the individual ticket and is required to be entered, scanned, or otherwise transmitted to a remote verification system, database, or point-of-sale terminal in order to render the ticket eligible for play or redemption, while the validation code—distinct in value and function from the activation code—serves as a secondary, independent identifier used exclusively to confirm the authenticity and payout eligibility of the ticket after the scratch-off varnish has been removed and the underlying game outcome revealed. The activation code and validation code are positioned on physically separate regions of the ticket, optionally on opposing faces or within separate perforated sub-sections, such that activation of the ticket (e.g., at time of sale) does not disclose or compromise the validation code, and disclosure of the validation code (e.g., at time of prize claim) does not permit retroactive activation of an unsold or unactivated ticket. This separation of functions ensures that a ticket which has not been properly activated through the designated verification channel cannot be fraudulently validated for prize redemption, even if the scratch-off varnish has been removed, thereby providing a dual-layer security architecture in which possession of the revealed game indicia alone is insufficient for redemption absent a confirmed, database-logged activation event tied to the ticket's unique activation code. The header portion of the card may further include static identifying information, including but not limited to a card serial number, game name, odds disclosure, and issuer information, printed in permanent, non-varnished ink, said header portion remaining attached to the substrate after individual tickets are detached so as to preserve a record of the batch or card of origin for audit and reconciliation purposes.

# PATENT APPLICATION

## TITLE OF INVENTION
**System and Method for Group Activation and Individual Redemption Tracking of Instant-Win Lottery Ticket Sheets**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to lottery ticket distribution and validation systems, and more particularly to a system and method for enabling the point-of-sale activation of a plurality of instant-win lottery tickets arranged on a single printed sheet as a unitary transaction, while maintaining discrete, individually addressable redemption status records for each constituent ticket within a centralized validation database.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Instant-win lottery tickets are conventionally distributed and activated as individual units, each bearing a unique identifier that is registered with a central lottery validation system at the point of sale. Retailers and consumers have expressed a need for a mechanism whereby multiple tickets—such as those pre-printed in a connected sheet, booklet, or perforated array—may be purchased and activated in a single transaction for administrative and commercial efficiency, without sacrificing the ability of the lottery operator to track, validate, and prevent duplicate redemption of each individual ticket.

Prior art systems generally require either (a) sequential individual scanning and activation of each ticket, which is time-consuming, or (b) bulk activation without granular tracking, which creates vulnerability to fraud, duplicate claims, or inventory discrepancies. There exists a need for a system that reconciles the commercial convenience of group-level activation with the security requirement of ticket-level redemption tracking.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides a system and method comprising:

1. A printed sheet substrate bearing a plurality of discrete instant-win lottery tickets, each ticket comprising a unique **primary ticket identifier** (e.g., a barcode, QR code, alphanumeric string, or RFID-encoded tag) and a concealed play-value indicium;

2. A **master sheet identifier**, printed or encoded upon the sheet substrate, which is cryptographically or relationally associated in a central database with each of the primary ticket identifiers of the tickets contained thereon;

3. A point-of-sale scanning and activation module configured to read the master sheet identifier and, upon a single scan event, transmit an activation request to a central validation server for **all associated primary ticket identifiers simultaneously**;

4. A central validation server comprising a relational database wherein each primary ticket identifier is stored as an individual record having its own activation status field and redemption status field, said records being linked to, but independently modifiable from, the master sheet identifier record; and

5. A redemption terminal or module configured to accept a single ticket (once separated from the sheet via perforation or cutting) and query the central validation server using only that ticket's primary ticket identifier, such that the redemption status of that individual ticket is updated (e.g., from "active-unclaimed" to "redeemed") without altering the redemption status of any other ticket sharing the same master sheet identifier.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### I. Physical Ticket Sheet Construction

In a preferred embodiment, the invention comprises a substrate, such as paper or synthetic card stock, upon which are printed a plurality of *N* discrete lottery ticket instances (where *N* is an integer greater than one), each said instance comprising:

- (a) a scratch-off or otherwise concealed play area containing randomly or pseudo-randomly generated prize-determining indicia;
- (b) a **primary ticket identifier**, printed in human-readable and/or machine-readable form (including but not limited to a linear barcode, two-dimensional matrix barcode, alphanumeric serial number, or embedded RFID/NFC chip), said identifier being unique across the entire population of tickets issued by the lottery operator;
- (c) perforation lines or other separation means disposed between adjacent ticket instances, enabling physical separation of individual tickets from the sheet without damage to the primary ticket identifier or play area of any ticket.

The sheet further comprises a **master sheet identifier**, distinct from any individual primary ticket identifier, disposed at a designated location on the sheet (e.g., a header region, margin, or reverse side), said master sheet identifier being machine-readable and unique to that specific sheet instance.

### II. Database Association Architecture

Prior to distribution, a central lottery database is populated with a data structure associating the master sheet identifier with each of the *N* primary ticket identifiers printed on that sheet, such as, by way of non-limiting example:

```
TABLE: Sheet_Registry
  Master_Sheet_ID (Primary Key)
  Sheet_Status (e.g., "unactivated" / "activated")
  Date_Printed
  Distribution_Batch_ID

TABLE: Ticket_Registry
  Primary_Ticket_ID (Primary Key)
  Master_Sheet_ID (Foreign Key, references Sheet_Registry)
  Ticket_Position_Index (e.g., position 1 through N on sheet)
  Activation_Status (e.g., "inactive" / "active")
  Redemption_Status (e.g., "unredeemed" / "redeemed" / "void")
  Prize_Value (populated or referenced upon validation)
  Timestamp_Activated
  Timestamp_Redeemed
```

This relational structure permits a **one-to-many relationship** wherein a single activation event directed at the Master_Sheet_ID field triggers a batch update operation across all *N* corresponding rows in the Ticket_Registry table, while preserving each row's independent capacity for subsequent, individualized modification.

### III. Group Activation Method

The method of group activation comprises the steps of:

**Step 1:** A retailer or point-of-sale terminal scans or otherwise reads the master sheet identifier disposed upon the uncut ticket sheet.

**Step 2:** The point-of-sale terminal transmits an activation request, comprising the master sheet identifier and a transaction timestamp, to the central validation server.

**Step 3:** The central validation server, upon receiving said activation request, performs a lookup operation in the Sheet_Registry table to confirm the master sheet identifier has not been previously activated.

**Step 4:** Upon confirmation, the central validation server executes a batch update query against the Ticket_Registry table, setting the Activation_Status field to "active" for all rows wherein the Master_Sheet_ID foreign key matches the scanned master sheet identifier, and populates the Timestamp_Activated field for each such row with the transaction timestamp.

**Step 5:** The central validation server transmits a confirmation signal to the point-of-sale terminal, indicating successful activation of all *N* tickets, and optionally causes a receipt to be printed reflecting the quantity and value of tickets activated.

Notably, in this step, **no Redemption_Status field is altered**, such fields remaining in their default "unredeemed" state for each individual ticket, thereby preserving the necessity of individual redemption verification at a later time.

### IV. Individual Redemption Method

Subsequent to group activation and physical separation of an individual ticket from the sheet (via the perforation means), the method of individual redemption comprises:

**Step 1:** A ticket holder presents a single, separated ticket bearing only its unique primary ticket identifier (the master sheet identifier being either omitted from the individual ticket portion, retained as a non-functional reference, or rendered inert upon separation, depending on the embodiment).

**Step 2:** A redemption terminal scans the primary ticket identifier and transmits a redemption request to the central validation server, said request comprising the primary ticket identifier alone (without reference to the master sheet identifier).

**Step 3:** The central validation server queries the Ticket_Registry table using the primary ticket identifier as the lookup key and retrieves the Activation_Status and Redemption_Status fields for that specific record only.

**Step 4:** If Activation_Status equals "active" and Redemption_Status equals "unredeemed," the server authorizes payment of the associated Prize_Value, updates the Redemption_Status field to "redeemed" for that individual record exclusively, and populates the Timestamp_Redeemed field.

**Step 5:** The server transmits a validation-confirmed signal to the redemption terminal, authorizing payout, while leaving the Redemption_Status fields of all other tickets sharing the same Master_Sheet_ID unaffected and independently queryable.

In this manner, though *N* tickets were activated in a single group transaction referencing only the master sheet identifier, each of the *N* tickets retains a fully independent redemption lifecycle, preventing duplicate redemption, enabling fraud detection (e.g., flagging anomalous redemption patterns across a single sheet), and preserving auditability.

### V. Alternative Embodiments

In an alternative embodiment, rather than a relational foreign-key structure, the association between the master sheet identifier and the *N* primary ticket identifiers may be encoded cryptographically, wherein the primary ticket identifier of each ticket is generated as a deterministic function (e.g., a cryptographic hash or HMAC) of the master sheet identifier concatenated with the ticket's positional index, such that a central server may verify the validity and sheet-membership of any presented primary ticket identifier without requiring a pre-populated lookup table, while still maintaining a separate mutable redemption-status record for each derived identifier.

In a further alternative embodiment, the master sheet identifier may be encoded in a distributed ledger (blockchain) structure, wherein the group activation event constitutes a single transaction that instantiates *N* child tokens, each corresponding to an individual ticket and each independently transferable and "burnable" upon redemption, without necessity of a centralized database.

In yet a further embodiment, the sheet may include a tear-off activation stub bearing the master sheet identifier separately from all ticket portions, such that the stub is retained by the retailer as a physical activation record while the individual tickets, bearing only their primary identifiers, are distributed to consumers.

---

**Claim 1.** A method for activating a plurality of instant-win lottery tickets as a single transaction while maintaining independent redemption tracking for each ticket, the method comprising:
providing a printed sheet comprising a plurality of *N* discrete lottery tickets, each ticket bearing a unique primary ticket identifier, and the sheet further bearing a master sheet identifier distinct from each primary ticket identifier;
storing, in a central database, a relational association between the master sheet identifier and each of the *N* primary ticket identifiers;

# Technical Disclosure: Multi-Ticket Game Sheet with Integrated Validation Code System

## Field of the Disclosure

This disclosure relates to instant-win lottery and promotional game products, specifically to a multi-ticket game sheet architecture incorporating cryptographically-linked validation codes that determine winning status while preventing duplicate or fraudulent redemption.

---

## 1. Background

Traditional instant-win game tickets are issued as single, independent units, each bearing its own scratch-off play area and validation code. In multi-ticket formats—where several individual tickets are printed on a single perforated sheet—prior art solutions have typically treated each ticket as an isolated unit, requiring separate database entries and separate validation transactions. This approach introduces several problems:

- **Redundant data storage** across a central validation system for tickets that share a common issuance batch.
- **Vulnerability to counterfeiting**, particularly when validation codes are generated using predictable sequential logic.
- **Inability to detect** whether a physical sheet has been tampered with (e.g., tickets removed and replaced, or a sheet re-assembled from mismatched sources).
- **Redemption race conditions**, where duplicate or cloned tickets are presented for payout at different retail terminals before the central system can flag them.

This disclosure describes a game sheet architecture and associated validation methodology that addresses these deficiencies.

---

## 2. Overview of the Game Sheet Structure

### 2.1 Physical Layout

The multi-ticket game sheet comprises:

- A **substrate sheet** divided into *N* individually perforated ticket segments (e.g., N = 4, 6, or 8), each separable along die-cut or micro-perforated lines.
- Each segment contains:
  - A **play area** (scratch-off latex or peel-away label) revealing symbols, numbers, or matching-game elements that determine the ticket's inherent win/loss outcome.
  - A **printed Ticket Validation Number (TVN)**, rendered in human-readable form and as a machine-readable barcode/QR code.
  - A **Sheet Identification Code (SIC)**, common to all tickets originating from the same parent sheet, printed in a fixed, non-scratch-off location on each segment.

- A **master sheet header region** (typically retained as a stub, or printed in the sheet margin) containing:
  - The **Sheet Master Code (SMC)** — a unique identifier for the entire sheet.
  - A **checksum/parity block** derived from all N individual TVNs.

### 2.2 Validation Code Composition

Each ticket's TVN is constructed as a composite value:

```
TVN = [SIC | POS | RNG | CRC]
```

Where:
- **SIC** (Sheet Identification Code): identifies the parent sheet batch, print run, and production facility.
- **POS** (Position Index): a 2–3 digit field indicating the ticket's position on the sheet (1 through N), which also encodes adjacency/sequence relationships used for tamper detection.
- **RNG**: a cryptographically generated random or pseudo-random segment unique to that ticket, sourced from a secure random number generator (SRNG) seeded independently for each sheet at time of print-file generation.
- **CRC**: a checksum computed over the SIC, POS, and RNG fields using a keyed hash function (e.g., HMAC-SHA256, truncated to a fixed field length for barcode compactness), using a private key held only by the game operator's validation server infrastructure.

This structure ensures that:
1. No two tickets—even across different sheets—share an identical TVN.
2. Any single-character alteration of SIC, POS, or RNG invalidates the CRC, causing immediate rejection at scan time.
3. The relationship between a ticket's POS and its SIC can be cross-referenced against a **sheet manifest** stored centrally, allowing detection of "orphaned" tickets whose sheet context does not match expected production records.

---

## 3. Determination of Winning Status

Winning status is determined through a **dual-layer verification model**, separating the *physical* reveal (visible to the player) from the *authoritative* determination (verified by the validation server).

### 3.1 Physical Play Area (Player-Facing)

The scratch-off or peel-away area encodes a game outcome using standard symbol-matching or numeric-match logic. This is a **preliminary indicator** only.

### 3.2 Server-Side Authoritative Determination

Upon redemption:

1. The TVN is scanned (via barcode/QR) or manually entered at a point-of-sale (POS) terminal or self-service redemption kiosk.
2. The terminal transmits the full TVN to the central Validation Server (VS) over an encrypted channel.
3. The VS:
   - Recomputes the CRC using the stored HMAC key and confirms it matches the submitted CRC (structural integrity check).
   - Looks up the TVN in the **Ticket Status Database (TSD)**, which stores, per ticket:
     - Predetermined prize tier (assigned at time of print-file generation, per the finite-pool/instant-win probability model),
     - Current status flag: `UNSOLD`, `ACTIVE`, `REDEEMED`, `VOID`.
   - If the TVN is `ACTIVE` and the CRC is valid, the VS returns the authoritative prize determination (including $0 for non-winning tickets) to the terminal.
   - The terminal display and the physical scratch reveal are cross-checked; a mismatch triggers a **manual review flag** rather than automatic payout, protecting against both counterfeit tickets and print-defect discrepancies.

This ensures the physical play area cannot, on its own, be forged to guarantee a payout—the server-side record is authoritative.

---

## 4. Duplicate Redemption Prevention

### 4.1 Atomic Status Transition

The core anti-duplication mechanism is an **atomic compare-and-set operation** on the TSD status field:

```
BEGIN TRANSACTION
  SELECT status FROM TSD WHERE tvn = :submitted_tvn FOR UPDATE
  IF status != 'ACTIVE':
      RETURN REJECT (reason: status)
  ELSE:
      UPDATE TSD SET status = 'REDEEMED', 
                     redeemed_at = NOW(), 
                     redeemed_terminal_id = :terminal_id
      RETURN ACCEPT (prize_tier)
COMMIT TRANSACTION
```

The row-level lock (`FOR UPDATE`) ensures that simultaneous redemption attempts from two different terminals—e.g., a legitimate ticket and a photocopied/cloned duplicate—cannot both succeed. The first request to acquire the lock transitions the status to `REDEEMED`; the second, arriving microseconds later, finds status already changed and is rejected.

### 4.2 Sheet-Level Cross-Validation

Because each TVN embeds the SIC and POS fields, the VS additionally maintains a **Sheet Manifest Table**, recording the expected set of TVNs for each SIC at print time. During redemption:

- The VS confirms the presented TVN's POS/SIC combination exists in the manifest and has not been previously flagged as "sheet compromised."
- If **more tickets are redeemed from a given SIC than the manifest allows** (e.g., attempted redemption of a duplicated/cloned ticket sharing a valid TVN from a stolen print file), the system flags the entire sheet for fraud investigation and freezes remaining unredeemed tickets from that SIC pending review.

### 4.3 Temporal and Geolocation Heuristics (Optional Layer)

As a supplementary fraud-detection measure, the VS may log redemption terminal geolocation and timestamp. Redemption attempts for the same TVN (or same SIC with anomalous POS patterns) occurring in disparate geographic regions within an implausible time window trigger automatic secondary review, independent of the atomic lock mechanism.

### 4.4 Void and Reversal Handling

If a ticket is voided (e.g., misprint, retailer error) prior to sale, its status is set to `VOID` in the TSD at activation time, preemptively blocking redemption regardless of a technically valid CRC—addressing the case where a ticket is physically valid but administratively invalid.

---

## 5. Sheet-Level Tamper Detection

Because the SMC checksum in the sheet header is computed as a keyed hash over all N TVNs at print time:

```
SMC_checksum = HMAC(key, TVN_1 || TVN_2 || ... || TVN_N)
```

any retailer-side audit or activation-scan process (performed when the sheet is first activated for sale) can validate that all N tickets are present, correctly ordered, and unaltered before the sheet is placed in active inventory. This prevents a scenario in which a bad actor swaps a losing ticket for a previously-identified winning ticket from a different sheet, since the substituted ticket's TVN would fail the SMC_checksum reconciliation.

---

## 6. Advantages

- **Single-pass sheet activation**: an entire sheet can be activated or voided as a unit via SMC validation, reducing retailer transaction overhead.
- **Cryptographic tamper resistance**: CRC/HMAC construction makes brute-force TVN forgery computationally infeasible without the private key.
- **Race-condition-safe redemption**: atomic status transition eliminates double-payout risk even under high concurrent load.
- **Layered fraud detection**: manifest-based sheet auditing catches systemic fraud (e.g., stolen print files) that individual TVN validation alone would miss.

---

## 7. Alternative Embodiments

- The POS field may be omitted in favor of encoding positional data directly into the RNG generation seed, at the cost of reduced tamper-detection granularity.
- The validation architecture may be extended to support **networked multi-sheet books** (books of sheets), with a Book Identification Code (BIC) superseding the SIC in the hierarchy, enabling three-tier reconciliation (Book → Sheet → Ticket).
- Blockchain or distributed-ledger backing of the TSD may be substituted for a centralized database in embodiments requiring multi-operator interoperability, with the atomic compare-and-set operation implemented via smart contract logic.

---

*This disclosure is provided for the purpose of establishing prior art and/or supporting a subsequent patent application. Claims may be drafted around any individual element or combination of elements described herein, including but not limited to the composite TVN structure, the atomic redemption transaction, and the sheet-level manifest reconciliation method.*

# EMBODIMENT DESCRIPTION

## Perforated Multi-Card Ticket Sheet with Simultaneous Activation Instant Win Gaming System

### FIELD OF THE EMBODIMENT

This embodiment relates to a lottery/gaming ticket assembly comprising a plurality of individually separable game cards joined along perforated boundaries, wherein each card contains independent instant-win indicia, and wherein an activation mechanism—such as a scratch-off layer, removable tab, or shared security seal—enables simultaneous or sequential activation of multiple cards from a single unitary sheet prior to separation.

---

### DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF AN EXEMPLARY EMBODIMENT

#### 1. General Construction of the Ticket Sheet

In one embodiment, the gaming product comprises a **substrate sheet (10)**, preferably formed of coated paperboard, synthetic polymer stock, or a paper/polymer laminate, having a first surface and an opposing second surface. The substrate sheet (10) is divided into a plurality of discrete **game card regions (12a, 12b, 12c ... 12n)**, each bounded by a **perforation line (14)** extending fully or partially through the thickness of the substrate.

The perforation lines (14) are configured to allow manual separation of each individual game card (12) from the remainder of the sheet (10) without damaging the printed indicia, the concealment layer, or any embedded security features. In one variant, the perforations comprise a series of micro-cuts spaced between 0.5 mm and 3 mm apart, arranged in a straight, curved, or die-cut decorative pattern (e.g., scalloped edges) to facilitate clean separation while maintaining structural integrity of the sheet during printing, handling, and distribution.

In an alternative embodiment, the perforation line (14) is replaced or supplemented by a partial-depth score line combined with an adhesive-release layer, permitting the individual cards to be peeled apart in addition to, or instead of, being torn.

#### 2. Individual Game Card Structure

Each game card region (12) includes:

- **(a) A play area (16)** printed with game indicia, which may include numbers, symbols, matching icons, or alphanumeric codes corresponding to a predetermined win/lose outcome determined at the time of manufacture (a "pre-determined outcome" instant lottery format);
- **(b) A concealment layer (18)**, such as a latex-based scratch-off coating, opaque removable label, or perforated pull-tab window, disposed over the play area (16) to prevent the outcome from being visible prior to activation;
- **(c) A validation code region (20)**, which may include a barcode, QR code, RFID chip, or alphanumeric string enabling electronic validation of the card independent of, or in conjunction with, the visual instant-win indicia;
- **(d) A card identifier (22)**, uniquely distinguishing each card (12) within the sheet (10) for tracking, auditing, and prize-pool reconciliation purposes.

#### 3. Simultaneous Activation Mechanism

A distinguishing feature of this embodiment is the **simultaneous activation mechanism (24)**, which enables a player to reveal, unlock, or activate the instant-win outcomes of two or more game cards (12) in a single action, prior to or independent of physical separation along the perforation lines (14).

Several alternative constructions of the simultaneous activation mechanism (24) are contemplated:

**(i) Shared Concealment Layer Embodiment:**
A single continuous concealment layer (18), such as a scratch-off latex coating, extends across multiple play areas (16a, 16b, 16c) of adjacent game cards (12) prior to separation. Scratching or removing a designated activation zone (26)—which may be centrally located relative to the grouped cards—simultaneously exposes the outcome indicia of all cards beneath the shared layer. In this embodiment, the perforation lines (14) are positioned beneath the shared concealment layer (18) such that separation of the individual cards may occur either before or after activation, without compromising the integrity of the revealed indicia.

**(ii) Shared Security Seal Embodiment:**
A single **tamper-evident security seal (28)** overlays a designated **activation strip (30)** spanning multiple card regions (12). The security seal (28) includes a frangible substrate that, upon removal, simultaneously breaks a common electrical, optical, or mechanical trigger associated with each underlying card, thereby "activating" the cards for validation purposes (e.g., enabling a validation code (20) to be read by a point-of-sale terminal, or arming an embedded chip for electronic outcome determination).

**(iii) Mechanical Linkage Embodiment:**
The game cards (12) are joined not only by perforation lines (14) but also by a **mechanical linkage tab (32)**—a small, non-perforated bridging section connecting an activation flap on each card. Pulling or removing the linkage tab (32) in a single motion simultaneously triggers a spring-loaded, chemically-reactive, or mechanically-actuated reveal window on each connected card, exposing the instant-win indicia of all linked cards at once.

**(iv) Electronic/RFID Activation Embodiment:**
Each game card (12) incorporates a passive RFID or NFC chip (34) linked to the validation code region (20). The sheet (10) further includes a **master activation chip (36)** or printed conductive trace connecting the individual chips (34) prior to separation. Passing the entire sheet (10), or a designated activation zone (26) thereof, near an activation terminal (e.g., at a retail point-of-sale) triggers a broadcast signal that simultaneously "unlocks" the electronic outcome status of all connected cards in a backend gaming server, even though the visual scratch-off layer (18) on each card may still require independent manual removal.

#### 4. Outcome Determination and Independence of Cards

Notwithstanding the simultaneous activation feature, each game card (12) retains an **independently predetermined outcome** established during the manufacturing/printing process, in accordance with a randomized or pseudo-randomized prize distribution algorithm applied across the full production run of sheets. Simultaneous activation does not imply correlated or dependent outcomes between cards; rather, it provides a convenience and engagement mechanism whereby a player may reveal multiple independent instant-win results through a single physical or electronic action.

In an alternative embodiment, the activation mechanism (24) may be configured to reveal outcomes **sequentially rather than simultaneously**, wherein activating a first card (12a) triggers a delayed or conditional activation window for a second card (12b), such delay being implemented via a time-release chemical layer, a mechanically staged tab system, or a software-enforced delay in the electronic embodiment.

#### 5. Perforation and Separation Variants

The perforation lines (14) may be configured in multiple patterns depending on the desired sheet layout:

- **Linear grid pattern:** cards (12) arranged in rows and columns, each separated by intersecting horizontal and vertical perforation lines;
- **Radial pattern:** cards (12) arranged around a central activation zone (26), with perforation lines extending radially outward, particularly suited to the shared concealment layer embodiment (i);
- **Strip pattern:** cards (12) arranged in a single row, connected end-to-end, suited to point-of-sale roll-fed dispensing systems.

The sheet (10) may further include a **header region (38)** or **border region (40)**, free of perforations, containing game rules, sheet-level barcodes, promotional information, or manufacturer identification, which may itself be detachable via an additional perforation line.

#### 6. Alternative Materials and Manufacturing Considerations

The substrate sheet (10) may be produced via offset lithography, flexographic printing, or digital printing, with the concealment layer (18) applied via a secondary latex-coating or lamination pass. The perforation lines (14) may be formed using rotary die-cutting, laser scoring, or reciprocating perforation tooling integrated into the web-fed production line, allowing high-throughput manufacture of multi-card sheets with consistent perforation depth and simultaneous-activation feature alignment.

---

### ADDITIONAL EMBODIMENTS AND VARIATIONS

It will be understood by a person skilled in the art that the number of game cards (12) per sheet (10) may vary from two to any practical number (e.g., 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, or more), and that the simultaneous activation mechanism (24) described above may be combined in hybrid form—for example, combining a shared concealment layer (embodiment (i)) with an RFID validation backend (embodiment (iv)) to provide both a physical and electronic simultaneous-activation experience. Furthermore, the specific shapes of the game cards (12), including but not limited to rectangular, circular, hexagonal, or novelty die-cut shapes, do not depart from the scope of this embodiment, provided that the perforation and simultaneous activation features described herein are retained.

This embodiment is illustrative only, and it is contemplated that various modifications—including changes in materials, activation triggers, perforation geometries, and the number and arrangement of game cards—may be made without departing from the spirit and scope of the invention as defined in the appended claims.
